utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Older male voice: "Wait, the house was not on fire a short while ago." Younger male voice: "A plane bombarded it. The plane just dropped a dozen of shells." Older voice: "And did it hit a truck as well?" Younger male voice: "Yes, it did, they are now on the houses." Now, my question is, Ms. Filipovic, if you can help us: Do you still say that there's no possibility that Serb planes caused any damage to buildings in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I told you before, in that locality where I was, there was no plane activity, although I could see on this video footage that the plane was there in the area of Bjelovac where houses were on fire. That's what I saw on this film.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just to be clear, though --

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that it is further up.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: During this time you were inside a house, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: People were shooting from the windows of the house, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So you weren't going up to the windows and looking out, were you?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that moment I no longer went to the window to look after I was detained.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm just going to play a tiny extra segment. I'm going to fast-forward to 0835 and then just play 30 seconds more.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I don't know if you can see on the monitor, Ms. Filipovic, but do you agree that we see there a bomb that the plane has just dropped; it's a speck in the middle of the screen. If not, don't worry. We'll play on to 9.20.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would you also agree that we can see the impact of that bomb dropping and jolting the camera and then see smoke rising from the damage caused by the bomb dropped by the plane?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you are drawing too many conclusions, Mr. Jones. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I mean, I would not agree with any one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But you see a bomb dropped, you see the camera jumps all over the place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but that's the cameraman. The smoke that I see, I don't know, I would be very surprised if all that smoke came out as a result of that explosion in the same second that the explosion takes place.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Certainly. I trust Your Honours will keep an open mind as to what caused the damage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There's certainly a bomb falling, you know, a bomb falling.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So we're finished with that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And incidentally now this is 3.20 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I don't wish to rehearse the evidence again of the plane in the air in the morning. I trust the point is taken that there was a plane dropping bombs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Definitely. Point taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you also told us yesterday that a person said to another person to burn down your house. And I want to be very clear about these two people. The person who said that your house should be burnt down, what was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: What else was he wearing? Can you give us more of a description than that? Any other features?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And it's right, isn't it, that you don't know whether this order, as you've described it, to burn down your house was actually executed by the person who was said to, do you?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we were leaving the house, as we were coming out of the house, one of the soldiers from the group said, Burn down the house. I did not turn around to see and I didn't dare to look back to see if the man was going at the same time to set the house on fire. But I heard definitely the words being said, Burn down the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So it's right, isn't it, that it could have been an empty menace which was never carried out?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't get your drift.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I withdraw that question. I want to move to the subject of when you were in Poloznik and you said that you heard people coming in all day with messages. Now, these people were very agitated, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think you told us that you heard some of the messages. Were they or weren't they of the following nature: First that there was a massive counter-attack coming back from the Serbs and that they were having to withdraw. Do you remember hearing messages of that nature?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, you said they were agitated or you agreed that were agitated. Weren't they agitated because they knew they had to get out of that area?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I see what you mean. I hadn't understood you very well before. When we moved to the house of Stevo Filipovic, I finally started hearing the sound of planes and they were afraid. They were moving around the house from one room to another. They were looking through the windows. Some were saying, in fact shouting, Go on, fire at him. And they were really in a state of panic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I was actually referring to later, though, in Poloznik when you said that people were coming with messages. And I was asking you whether you gathered from those messages that they were in difficulty and that they had to pull out.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I was not aware of the content of the those messages and I didn't know what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. You said that there was a radio in Ramiz's house. Wasn't it a small, improvised, battery-operated gadget, nothing very impressive. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain the way I remember it, what it looked like. It was perhaps more than 50 centimetres high, not very wide, 40 centimetres, not more. It was plugged into a battery, a car battery. It had a headset plugged into it and there were a lot of wires and cables around it. That's what I remember. I also remember it was green.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It was attached to a car battery -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you mention meeting Zulfo in Ramiz's house, and you said that you knew him because he used to come to your father's house. Now, can you tell us roughly when he came to your father's house? How many years before the war, let's take it that way.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in the '80s.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Could you be a bit more specific. Are we talking about 1981, 1985, 1989? How old were you when you saw Zulfo?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And before that, when you saw Zulfo at your father's house, how old were you roughly?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a young girl. I think I was going to primary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You say you recognised him from that period of, what, 14, 15 years beforehand?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, dealing with the period before you arrived in Srebrenica from, say, the 14th to about the 19th of December 1992, wasn't there massive fighting in that whole area, by which I mean the broader Bjelovac area, from Voljevica, Zaluzje, Pirici, Sase, fighting in that whole area?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand you very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Perhaps I can approach it by looking at D45 again, because I'm coming to that in any event. If we look firstly at number 11 we see that a Sretan Djokanovic died in Kostanovici on the 17th of December, 1992. Now, Kostanovici is on the road to Sase, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would you agree that is in the broad Bjelovac area. It's in your local area that you're familiar with?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with that area, but that's the area of Sase.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. If you look at 253 on that list, you see Zeljko Knezovic who died on the 16th of December, 1992, in Kunjarac. Now, is that in your area?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bjelovac is separate. Kunjarac is on the other side of the hill from Bjelovac. And this man or young man or boy that you mentioned is a person I absolutely don't know. Knezovic, I don't know him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just to ask you this, really. How far would you estimate Kunjarac is from Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to three kilometres away, not more.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, just a couple more names. Number 295, Stanoje Maric who died in Voljevica on the 22nd of December, 1992. Voljevica is the next village up from Bjelovac, isn't it, towards Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This person I don't know either.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And then finally 342, we see Stojan Milic died in Sase on the 15th of December, 1992. Sase is but a few kilometres --

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, not the same what?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I meant is I don't know this person either.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's fine. It was really to make this point, and I'm going back to the question I asked you, is aren't you aware, or are you aware that between the 14th of the December and let's say for the next week or so, there was intensive combat between Serbs and Muslims in this whole area, Sase, Bjelovac, Voljevica, Kunjarac. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I didn't know that. I wasn't aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you find that out later?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't try to find out. I didn't make inquiries, and I didn't even learn accidentally from anybody else that fighting was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I would like to show a short segment of D97, just a minute and a half of that video.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If we freeze there firstly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Ms. Filipovic, you're from the Bjelovac area, you're from Azlica originally, and I gather it appears that you know many people from the Sase mine. So I want you to tell us first if you recognise this area.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You don't recognise that as being Voljevica?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And tell us, either for the last segment or the next segment, whether you recognise any of the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And so we'll play a bit more.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just looking firstly at that soldier in the picture, do you agree that he's wearing a "kokada" [phoen] on his cap?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's unclear. I can't ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We'll just play a short segment of the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So just freezing there. It says there that's Commander Borivoje Tesic being interviewed. Do you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you agree that the soldiers we've seen are Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know that they are Serbs or Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We hear there or we see a mention of connecting forces in Bjelovac/Kunjarac. From the messages you heard when you were in Poloznik, did you hear Muslims saying how Serb forces were attacking from Voljevica to Bjelovac in order to recapture Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. No. I didn't hear the content of the messages.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. We're finished with that exhibit. Just a few more questions. I'll probably be ten minutes, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You told us yesterday how in order to get to Srebrenica on the 18th December, 1992, you were driven through Bjelovac in a yellow Mercedes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And that Mercedes, as far as you were concerned, was that Mis's car or as far as you knew?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't his car in the first place. He himself said that he had taken the car from Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But from then on -- I withdraw that question. Did Mrki sometimes use that Mercedes as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know that he never used it, or you don't know whether he used it or not?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the way to Srebrenica, Mis was driving the car. When we were in Srebrenica and when we went to Solocusa, it was again Mis, mouse, who drove that car.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, on that drive I think you told us you had time to see your house and even in some detail, because you told us that you could see that even the woodwork was destroyed?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I paid attention specially to see that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So the car was driving on at quite a slow pace then, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not particularly fast or particularly slow, medium speed. But I still tried to look closely as we were passing by.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And this is the road which is along the Drina facing Serbia, and you say you were on that road on the 18th of December, 1992, without any problems?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But I'm going to put a suggestion to you which is that that's completely untrue, that that road was never controlled by the Muslims during the whole war, that it was intensively shelled from Serbia for days after the Bjelovac attack, and that any yellow car driving leisurely along would have a sitting duck for Serb shelling, Serb artillery. That's my suggestion. So I'd ask if you maintain that you did take that road?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: With the usher's assistance, I would like to put a map on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In the meantime, Ms. Filipovic, can you tell us whether you went by car even from Poloznik to Bjelovac. Was that part of your trip by car?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We travelled all the time in that same car to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It is my suggestion, and again I'm -- it is a suggestion, that the car could not even pass from Poloznik to Bjelovac because that road was blocked. You said it did pass from Poloznik to Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we were travelling there were no barriers, no checkpoints, on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My suggestion to you is that the route you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Roadblocks; interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My suggestion is the route you in fact took to get to Srebrenica was we went on a macadam, or dirt road from Poloznik to Predola, to Dimnici, Stozerska and then to Srebrenica, and that that was a road which the Muslims took to get to Srebrenica during the war. You say you didn't take that route? Sorry --

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll repeat the villages because I think it wasn't interpreted: Poloznik to Predola, to Dimnici, to Stozerska, and then to Srebrenica. Isn't that the route you in fact took?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would you agree that the following places were in Serb hands, were being fought over on the 18th of December, 1992, or thereabouts: Sase, Neskovici, Lasovac and Kostanovici?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Kostanovici, let's just take that one. Do you say that that was taken by Muslim forces in December 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. But when we were travelling to Srebrenica, Bjelovac, Zaluzje -- sorry, Bjelovac, Biljaca, Prisoje, Kostanici, Sase we passed by without any problem, not encountering a single roadblock. We passed smoothly all the way to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And neither Mis or Mrki nor anyone in the car expressed concern that they would be ambushed on that road, on the Sase road?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I put it to you, Ms. Filipovic, that in fact you've told us you went via Bjelovac purely so you can claim to have had a view of your house and that you didn't take that route. I understand you'll deny that and I'll move to another area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you better move to another area.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm just waiting for the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Ms. Filipovic, you referred to yesterday seeing a column of people. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Referring to a column of people and it was suggested to you, I think, that these were all soldiers. So I want to be clear. I think the number that was mentioned was 2.000. You're not saying, are you, that you saw 2.000 men all in uniform, every one of them with a rifle or some weapon?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. But I -- that was when I was in Poloznik in Ramo's [as interpreted] house where we were staying.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Didn't you see a column of civilians, men, women, and children, fleeing from Bjelovac and going towards Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You do know, though, don't you, from your time in Srebrenica that a lot of food was captured by civilians in Bjelovac, which kept a lot of hungry people fed for a while during that winter?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm clear about that, although this is not something that I actually saw. It is only natural they should be expected to go after food.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Finally, let's just clarify a couple of matters with regard to Srebrenica and your stay there. Isn't Solocusa where you stayed more like four kilometres from Srebrenica than one or two kilometres or whatever was suggested?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult to say exactly, but it's quite near and it's at the entrance to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: How long would it take you to walk from Solocusa to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would take between 20 and 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I don't know if it's just me, but I'm not getting very good sound. Maybe it's just me. Anyway, I've only got a few more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have no problems with my sound at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you were asked yesterday about being interrogated in you were Srebrenica. The people who asked you questions, they weren't unpleasant, though, were they? They just asked you questions?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did ask us questions. But they were also quite angry, and threats were made simply because we were unable to answer the questions which they were asking us.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm looking at a prior statement of yours. I just have to check which one it was. But haven't you said in the past that the behaviour of the people asking you questions was quite correct? I'm looking at the 1994 statement, ERN 03090987: "Their behaviour during the questioning was correct." Do you agree that their behaviour was correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the Srebrenica SUP, the former SUP, yes, that was the case. However, when we gave a statement at Hamed's, he was angry. And I remember him saying, Of course you know, of course you know what's going on, and sooner or later you'll have to tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Finally just a few questions on the documents which you were asked about yesterday, and it really is about four questions. You were shown some documents yesterday, starting with Exhibit P470, and it's 02075729 dated 28th February 1993. Isn't it right that you weren't interviewed or asked questions at the end of February 1993, were you?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't understand. Can you please repeat this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. When you were asked questions, as you've just described, that wasn't at the end of February 1993, was it?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure -- interviewed by who? Asked questions by who? And when exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The Muslims in Srebrenica, when they asked you questions, when was that.

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the first and second day following our arrival in Srebrenica, on the first and second day.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So December 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When we arrived in Srebrenica, we were taken straight to the building adjacent to the town hall and that was where we were questioned. The very next day we were brought back, questioned there, and also in the former SUP building of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And now -- I don't know if this is necessarily something you can help us with, but if we look at that document it has the number 12/1993. And if we look at Exhibit P469, the number is 16/1993, but it's dated the 3rd of February, 1993 -- yes, sorry, P469 and P470.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: These are the ones we saw yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honour, the point really is that one comes earlier in time than the other one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I don't think you need to hammer that because we pointed that out ourselves, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. And also to take matters shortly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There can also be a very simple explanation to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we make the points we make about the documents, and obviously we trust they're taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Looking at P470 as well, 02075729, that's dated 28th of February, 1993, and I'll just ask you if you agree that that's recommending an exchange and proposing to expedite it when in fact you and your children have been released before that date. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly the date of the exchange in February, but I can tell you for sure that it was February.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. You noted that one document had the wrong information about your daughter's birthday and who their father is. As far as you recollect, did you give the correct information to whoever was interviewing you?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: As far as the --

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Finally, a final question, turning to your exchange, isn't it right that a large number of Serbs -- Serbs were exchanged alive for dead Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, 20 Serbs who were alive were exchanged -- and one dead body were exchanged for dead bodies of Muslims. No one remained alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Jones. Is there re-examination? MR. DI FAZIO: One issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: It will take -- very, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Take your time. There's no problem at this point in time. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I'll finish briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I just want to ask you about one topic. You were asked questions by Mr. Jones regarding the attackers on the 14th of December, 1992, and where they came from, and you identified a number of people who came from Sase, Voljevica, and Zaluzje. And you've told us already -- we've already heard your evidence about how on the 14th you were in your house and then Stevo Filipovic's house and then in the evening taken off to Poloznik, okay? Now my question is this - and you may be able to answer it very, very simply - can you -- do you know, and if you don't know, say so, but do you know if there were other Muslim attackers in other houses apart from those in your house with you and apart from the ones who were in Stevo Filipovic's house with you?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know at the time. The only thing I knew was about our house because I was there, and later when we crossed to Stevo Filipovic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: So the position is you simply can't tell this Trial Chamber if there were many other Muslim attackers in other houses or whether there were no other Muslim attackers in other houses?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not able to see whether there were any in the other houses because I was in my house throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you very much. MR. DI FAZIO: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Eser has got some questions for you, Madam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Madam Stojanovic, with regard to the house, your house, which was -- which you found burned, now you told us when this soldier or this person said, Let's burn down the house, that you did not look back so you did not realise whether it was really burnt at that moment. That's correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now, from your own house you moved to Stevo Filipovic's house. Now -- and while you have been in Stevo Filipovic's house, did you have a chance to look to your own house?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because there was no direct view on my house from Stevo's house. Not a single window faced that way. And there were houses between Stevo Filipovic's house and my house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you. Before I put my next question to you I would like -- have to ask the Defence, when you told the witness that it was untrue that she could have come from Bjelovac to Srebrenica, you told the Court that this road was never controlled by Muslims. Now, is this only a contention or has this brought into evidence that it was never controlled by Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's a suggestion which we -- yes, which we obviously intend to address during our Defence case, that that road was not used by Muslims. They would take another route to get to Srebrenica because of the dangers I alluded to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: But at this moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's a suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, my question to the witness. On which way would you normally go from Bjelovac to Srebrenica, in normal times? Which road would you take?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would go via Bratunac and then on to Srebrenica, under those circumstances. That was a sealed road, an asphalt road, with buses and cars taking that road to Srebrenica. The road between Bjelovac and Poloznik is a dirt track, a macadam track, and it is not particularly fit for traffic. For example, miners who lived in Poloznik and in Pirici, many of them worked at the mine, and in order to get to Loznica/Rijeka, or rather Bjelovac, they would drive in a van and then take a bus from Bjelovac to the mine itself, which means that not even the bus could go. We had our own miners' bus, but it couldn't go to those villages to pick those miners up simply because there was not road that was fit for bus traffic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... during this trip that you took from Poloznik to Srebrenica, this road you described to us, was it already known to you or did you go it for the first time that night?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To a certain extent, yes, my husband was from Loznica; he had been born there. This is a road that goes to Poloznik and I would take part of that road, one section of that road, on my way to Loznica. It is the same road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now, the last question. When you have been taken from your -- from Stevo Filipovic's house to go to this other place, what have you been told? Have you been told the reason why you were taken from this place to somewhere else or have you been just ordered that you should go with these people to the other place?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We simply went along. I don't remember that a specific order was issued, but they went and we came with them. We left Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now, my question was: Had you been given a reason why you should leave your -- Bjelovac and you said you should go to another place. Have you been given a reason for leaving the -- Stevo Filipovic's house and to follow these people to another place?

utterances.speaker: MIRA STOJANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. They didn't say anything. We just left and headed for Poloznik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Judge Eser. I do not have questions for you, Madam, which basically means that your testimony comes to an end here. On behalf of Judge Brydensholt and Judge Eser and on my own behalf and also on behalf of the Tribunal, I should like to thank you for having come over to give testimony in this case. You will now be escorted out of the courtroom by Madam Usher and you will be attended to by the rest of the staff of the Tribunal, who will assist you in -- to make it possible to return back home at the earliest opportunity. On behalf of everyone present here, I wish to -- wish you a safe journey back home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I take it that we will resume on Monday. Tomorrow is a UN holiday, Eid Al-Adha. And we will resume on Monday with the testimony of witness number 25. MR. DI FAZIO: That's fine. Your Honours, there was an issue raised by Mr. Siller regarding certain documents and exhibits. I respectfully suggest that we deal with this at a later point next week. There's nothing urgent as far as I can see. And I just need to get my -- need to understand more precisely what is going on before I can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Have a nice weekend. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
